subsystems.name: Thermoelectric module
subsystems.role: converts a temperature difference into a small voltage via the Seebeck effect.
parts: p-type and n-type semiconductor legs (often bismuth telluride alloys)

subsystems.name: Thermal path
subsystems.role: maintains the temperature gradient between skin and air.

subsystems.name: Power management
subsystems.role: boosts the very low voltage and charges a storage element.

subsystems.name: Energy storage
subsystems.role: buffers intermittent output so the load sees steady power.

subsystems.name: Wearable housing
subsystems.role: holds the module against the skin comfortably and prevents heat from bypassing the generator.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise thermoelectric material
buildSteps.detail: Bismuth telluride alloys are melted or sintered, then doped to create p-type and n-type ingots.

buildSteps.title: Form the legs
buildSteps.detail: Ingots are diced into small pillars, and electrical contacts are prepared on their ends.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the module
buildSteps.detail: P-type and n-type legs are soldered alternately between ceramic plates so their voltages add in series while heat flows in parallel.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the thermal path
buildSteps.detail: A skin-facing pad and an air-facing heat sink are attached to the module with thermally conductive but electrically insulating layers.

buildSteps.title: Design power electronics
buildSteps.detail: A boost converter is built to start at tens of millivolts and track the module's maximum power point.

buildSteps.title: Integrate storage
buildSteps.detail: A thin-film battery or supercapacitor is connected through a charge controller to store harvested energy.

buildSteps.title: Package the wearable
buildSteps.detail: Module, electronics and storage are encapsulated in a flexible band with insulation around the edges to stop heat short-circuiting.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Power output is measured at different skin temperatures, air temperatures and contact pressures to tune the electronics.

prerequisites.tech: Thermoelectric materials with high figure of merit near body temperature
prerequisites.why: bismuth telluride alloys are already used in commercial Peltier coolers and generators.
rigid modules are brittle and bulky; conformal versions are needed for comfortable wear.
the output voltage is only millivolts, so harvesting circuits must start at very low input.
they store small amounts of energy in a wearable form factor.
a heat sink must reject heat to air without making the device bulky or uncomfortable.

pathway.milestone: niche body-heat powered devices such as thermoelectric watches and sensor nodes
pathway.unlocks: battery-free or extended-runtime wearables for specialised uses.

pathway.milestone: flexible, printed thermoelectric modules with improved efficiency
pathway.unlocks: conformal bands that produce usable milliwatts from body heat.

pathway.milestone: integration with ultra-low-power chips and thin-film storage
pathway.unlocks: self-powered fitness trackers and IoT sensors that trickle-charge themselves.

pathway.milestone: slow charging of very small consumer devices such as earbuds
pathway.unlocks: reduced reliance on wall charging for micro-electronics, within thermodynamic limits.
